title: Rapid mixing for Gibbs samplers for quantum spin systems with all-to-all interactions
abstract: Understanding when quantum many-body systems rapidly converge to thermal equilibrium is a central problem in quantum statistical mechanics. While spatial locality provides powerful tools for systems with an underlying geometry, fully connected models require estimates that accommodate interactions between every pair of spins. We study Gibbs-state preparation for two-local quantum Hamiltonians on arbitrary interaction graphs, including fully connected systems, via Lindblad dynamics that satisfies Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. Our approach is based on a quantum analogue of the classical Dobrushin condition, which controls the influence of local perturbations on the rest of the system. Using the quantum Wasserstein distance of order $1$, we quantify how these perturbations propagate under the dynamics and derive contraction estimates in a high-temperature regime controlled by the maximum total interaction strength per site. These estimates require no assumptions on spatial geometry or graph growth and yield mixing times logarithmic in the system size and the inverse error tolerance, uniformly over all initial states.
summary: This paper establishes conditions for rapid thermalization in quantum spin systems, particularly those with all-to-all interactions. By adapting the Dobrushin condition using quantum Wasserstein distance, the authors prove that the mixing time scales only logarithmically with system size. This result is significant because it provides robust bounds for Gibbs state preparation without assuming any specific spatial geometry for the interactions.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the conditions under which quantum many-body systems rapidly converge to their thermal equilibrium state (Gibbs state).
main_result: The authors derive a sufficient condition ensuring that the mixing time for Gibbs state preparation is logarithmic in the system size, $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, even for fully connected systems.
method: The approach uses a quantum analogue of the classical Dobrushin condition, quantifying perturbation propagation via the quantum Wasserstein distance of order 1.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-body quantum spin Hamiltonians on arbitrary interaction graphs, including fully connected models, evolving under Lindblad dynamics satisfying KMS detailed balance.

important_parameters: The inverse temperature ($ eta$) and the maximum total interaction strength per site ($\Lambda$), which controls the high-temperature regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to two-body qubit interactions and requires the temperature to be sufficiently high relative to the interaction strength ($ eta\Lambda < 1/100$).
paper_structure: The paper builds upon the Dobrushin-to-mixing framework, analyzing the dynamics via the quantum Wasserstein distance to derive contraction estimates for the Gibbs state preparation.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, geometry-independent bounds on thermalization times for complex quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
